areas.title: God, faith and reason
areas.line: The arguments for God's existence, set out step by step, with their strongest critics.

areas.title: Can we trust the text of the New Testament?
areas.line: Manuscripts, variants and disputed passages, and what the evidence shows.

areas.title: Who wrote the Gospels and the New Testament, when, and who chose the books
areas.line: Who wrote the Gospels and the letters, when, and how the church came to its list of books.

areas.title: Contradictions and hard passages
areas.line: The census, the two genealogies, the death of Judas, the day of the crucifixion and the numbers in Kings and Chronicles.

areas.title: The historical Jesus and the resurrection
areas.line: Whether Jesus lived, what he claimed, the empty tomb, the appearances and the virgin birth.

areas.title: The Old Testament: history, archaeology, violence and law
areas.line: The exodus, the conquest, Daniel, the flood, the law and the charge of an angry God.

areas.title: Science
areas.line: Galileo, miracles, the beginning of the universe, evolution, and what science can and can't settle.

areas.title: Evil, suffering and judgment
areas.line: The problem of evil in its logical and evidential forms, natural evil, God's hiddenness and hell.

areas.title: Morality, sexuality and the church's record
areas.line: The Crusades, the Inquisition, slavery and conquest, abuse and its cover-up, and the charge that religion poisons everything.

areas.title: Other religions, and those who never heard
areas.line: Whether all religions say the same thing, Jesus as the only way, and those who never heard.
